# The vehicle table {#sec-vehicle-table}

```{r}
source("R/book.R")
dd <- read_pipeline("outputs", "data_dictionary.csv")
n_rows <- dd$n_rows[1]
year_cols <- grepl("_[0-9]{4}$", dd$column_name)
years <- sort(unique(as.integer(sub(".*_", "", dd$column_name[year_cols]))))
```

The vehicle table, `vehicles_enhanced.parquet`, is the most detailed CARS
product: one row for each of `r fmt_n(n_rows)` vehicles, with
`r nrow(dd)` columns. This chapter explains how it is organised and how to read
it. Every column is described in the [data dictionary](dictionary/index.qmd).

## Parquet

The table is stored as a [Parquet](https://parquet.apache.org/) file, a
compressed column-based format designed for large tables. You do not need to
load the whole file to use it: tools such as DuckDB read only the columns and
rows a query needs, so a count of vehicles by fuel reads a few hundred
megabytes, not 9 GB, and takes seconds. @sec-getting-started explains how to
set this up.

## One row per vehicle, one column per year

The table is *wide*. Characteristics that do not change, such as make and
fuel, appear once. Things that change from year to year appear as one column
per year, `r min(years)` to `r max(years)`:

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `mileage_YYYY` | Miles driven in the year |
| `legit_mileage_YYYY` | `TRUE` if the mileage is judged plausible; blank if not assessed |
| `pca_YYYY` | Postcode area of testing, or `unborn`, `unknown` or `dead` (@sec-lifecycle) |

For example, `mileage_2019` and `pca_2019` describe 2019. Many analyses need
the data *long* instead, with one row per vehicle per year;
@sec-examples-code shows how to reshape it.

## How columns are named

The column names follow a convention that tells you where each value comes
from:

| Pattern | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| ends `_DVSA` | As supplied by DVSA | `fuel_DVSA`, `engineSize_DVSA` |
| ends `_DVLA` | As returned by the DVLA Vehicle Enquiry Service | `co2Emissions_DVLA`, `euroStatus_DVLA` |
| ends `_ANON` | As supplied in the anonymised MOT data | `test_class_ANON` |
| no suffix, lower case | Made by the pipeline: cleaned, harmonised or derived | `fuel`, `engine_cc`, `co2`, `make_final` |
| ends `_src` | Where the harmonised value of that name came from | `co2_src` |
| ends `_check` | The result of a consistency check | `fuel_check`, `euro_check` |
| ends `_method` | How a make or model was matched | `model_method` |
| starts `scope_` | Why the vehicle is included | `scope_mileage` |

::: {.callout-tip title="Supplied or harmonised?"}
For most purposes use the harmonised columns (`fuel`, `engine_cc`, `co2`,
`euro_status` and so on): they are more complete, consistent and corrected. Use
the supplied columns to reproduce official figures exactly, or to check that a
result does not depend on the pipeline's choices.
:::

## Groups of columns

```{r}
#| label: tbl-column-groups
#| tbl-cap: "The columns of the vehicle table, by group."
fam <- function(x) {
  ifelse(grepl("^(mileage|legit_mileage|pca)_[0-9]{4}$", x), "Year by year",
  ifelse(grepl("^scope_|^total_mileage$", x), "Scope",
  ifelse(grepl("^(registration_(DVSA|DVLA|clean)$|plate_|vanity|dup_vrm|vehicle_id)", x), "Identity and number plate",
  ifelse(grepl("^(make|model|derivative|dft_|body_type)", x), "Make, model and body type",
  ifelse(grepl("^(n_VES|first_VES|last_VES|is_error|error|collectionDate|plate_ever|ever_|v5C_|change_in|dvla_match|dvla_evidence)", x), "DVLA lookup and record match",
  ifelse(grepl("(Date|date|_year|Year|Registration_DVLA|artEnd)", x), "Dates",
  ifelse(grepl("_(DVSA|DVLA|ANON)$", x), "Attributes as supplied",
  "Attributes harmonised by the pipeline")))))))
}
dd$group <- fam(dd$column_name)
order_groups <- c("Identity and number plate", "Make, model and body type",
                  "Attributes harmonised by the pipeline",
                  "Attributes as supplied", "Dates",
                  "DVLA lookup and record match", "Scope", "Year by year")
g <- do.call(rbind, lapply(order_groups, function(k) {
  cols <- dd$column_name[dd$group == k]
  shown <- if (k == "Year by year") {
    "mileage_YYYY, legit_mileage_YYYY, pca_YYYY"
  } else paste(cols, collapse = ", ")
  data.frame(Group = k, Columns = length(cols), Names = shown)
}))
kable(g, row.names = FALSE)
```

## Completeness

The table keeps vehicles for which little is known, rather than dropping them,
so how complete a column is varies a great deal. The data dictionary gives the
share missing for every column. Some patterns to know:

```{r}
pm <- setNames(dd$pct_missing, dd$column_name)
```

- **DVSA columns are nearly complete**, because every vehicle comes from the
  DVSA download. `engineSize_DVSA` is the exception, missing for
  `r pm["engineSize_DVSA"]`%.
- **DVLA columns are missing for about `r round(pm["make_DVLA"])`%** of
  vehicles, those for which no DVLA record was found. Most of these left the
  register years ago. Some DVLA fields are rare even when a record exists:
  `euroStatus_DVLA` is missing for `r pm["euroStatus_DVLA"]`%.
- **The harmonised columns fill most gaps**: `co2` is missing for
  `r pm["co2"]`% against `r pm["co2Emissions_DVLA"]`% for
  `co2Emissions_DVLA`, and `euro_status` for `r pm["euro_status"]`% against
  `r pm["euroStatus_DVLA"]`%.
- **Year-by-year columns are blank in most years for most vehicles**, because
  a vehicle is only on the road for part of the period. `mileage_2019` is
  blank for `r pm["mileage_2019"]`% of vehicles.

## The vehicles included

A vehicle is included if there is evidence that it existed at any point from
2005 (@sec-pipeline). The table therefore includes vehicles that were scrapped
in 2006, vehicles first registered in 2025 that have never been tested, and
everything in between. Any analysis of a particular year must first select the
vehicles relevant to that year, usually those *observed* in it: those with a
real postcode area in `pca_YYYY`.
